body:
POSSIBLE REAL DATA — THE OWNER POINTED AT AN AUTOBIOGRAPHICAL INTERVIEW DATASET. Assessment, with
the blocker stated up front.

THE DATASET: Fossard, M., Sandoz, M., Cordonier, N., & Schaffner, E. (2025), "Autobiographical
interview (Version 1.0)", UNINE data service, on SWISSUbase. Depositor: Université de Neuchâtel,
Institut des Sciences logopédiques; PI Marion Fossard.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT KIND OF DATA, and it is a strikingly close fit:
  - IT IS THE AUTOBIOGRAPHICAL INTERVIEW (Levine et al. 2002) -- the exact instrument our
    `interview` module targets. Our BirthdayInterview fixture is a SYNTHETIC version of this.
  - VERBATIM TRANSCRIPTS. Six personal narratives per participant: two remote past, two near past,
    two future. That directly exercises design rule 5, discourse time != story-world time != recall
    time, on real productions rather than authored ones.
  - SCORED ON INTERNAL (EPISODIC) VERSUS EXTERNAL (SEMANTIC) DETAILS. That is OUR ESTIMAND
    VOCABULARY, and it means there are HUMAN SCORES to calibrate against -- the benchmark we have
    never had. Today's measured baseline says every number we publish is a property of our own
    prose; this is the thing that changes that sentence.

THE BLOCKER, AND IT IS DECISIVE: IT IS NOT PUBLICLY AVAILABLE. Search results state the data is
available from Prof. Fossard on SWISSUbase (project 20962) but is RESTRICTED FOR PRIVACY REASONS.
The catalogue's public pages do not state the licence, access conditions, or redistribution terms
at all -- I tried the usage-licence path and it 404s, and the study overview omits ethics, consent
and anonymisation entirely.

TWO THINGS I COULD NOT RESOLVE AND WILL NOT GUESS:
  1. LANGUAGE. The dataset overview says English. The group's 2025 publications using this material
     are about FRENCH SPEAKERS. Either there are two datasets, or the overview's language field is
     wrong, or I am conflating records. Somebody must check before anyone plans around "English".
  2. POPULATION. The associated publications concern APHASIA and ALZHEIMER'S participants. Clinical
     populations are a materially more sensitive category than healthy-participant recall, and our
     admission checklist does not currently specify what that requires.

NOBODY SHOULD ATTEMPT TO FETCH THIS. Not a clone, not a sample, not one transcript for a probe. I
ruled this morning that participant recall text is barred until the owner records an REB basis, and
that pseudonymisation is not consent. This is precisely that case, with a clinical population on
top.

WHAT ONLY THE OWNER CAN DO: this needs direct contact with Prof. Fossard and a data-use agreement.
The owner is a cognitive neuroscientist at Baycrest/Rotman and would be the named researcher on any
such agreement; no agent here can negotiate it and none should try.

IF IT IS OBTAINED, docs/design/story-text-admission-checklist.md gets its first real exercise, and
sections 1, 2 and 4 are ready. SECTION 3 -- human-subject provenance -- WILL NEED EXTENDING for
clinical data: consent scope for secondary analysis, whether derived scores may be published, and
whether anything may be redistributed at all, which for a privacy-restricted dataset is probably no.

I have not filed a bead. This is an owner action with a research-ethics dimension, not a task.
